repo_prior_art.cite: none; the Stat catalogue has no rare-event PN coverage kernel

published_prior_art.cite: TianWu2025 gives regular efficient PN inference; ZhangWangMiao2025 gives efficient inference for generally partially identified PN bounds, not rare-count point-PN inversion.
TianWu2025 supplies the regular monotone-PN EIF and efficient limit; the triangular-array effective-count extension is a plausible but narrower extension.
McGrathBurke2024 studies rare-binomial interval width and coverage; the guarded PN-score bound is distinct but conservative and not a matched frontier.
GleserHwang1987 concerns finite-expected-diameter impossibility in zero-information ratio-like models, not a bounded monotone-PN Poisson likelihood-ratio frontier.
GleserHwang1987 supplies a general expected-diameter impossibility template; the bounded monotone-PN two-point specialization is not stated there.
Huwang1995 studies non-uniform coverage of an approximate binomial interval; the mixed causal multinomial Poisson--Gaussian boundary is a routine specialization once the PN submodel is fixed.
MikushevaSun2022 develops weak-IV-robust AR test inference, not learned marked-Poisson calibration for PN.

novelty_flags.label: literature_map / McGrathBurke2024
novelty_flags.one_line: McGrathBurke2024 compares rare-binomial interval coverage and relative margin of error; it does not itself document a general Gaussian rare-binomial calibration failure, so reserve that claim for Huwang1995 or restate McGrath--Burke as motivation.

soundness_flags.label: def:clipped-learners / lem:learning-rates
soundness_flags.one_line: The construction says the outcome least-squares fit uses all training observations, which estimates E[Y|X] rather than m_0(x)=E[Y|A=0,X=x); specify fitting on A=0 training observations or an equivalent weighted regression.

soundness_flags.label: def:rare-pn-class / thm:uniform-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: M_n is declared a class of observed-data laws P_n but includes consistency, ignorability, and monotonicity stated using unobserved potential outcomes; define it as observed laws admitting a full-data extension satisfying those conditions.

soundness_flags.label: lem:lf-membership
soundness_flags.one_line: The explicit least-favorable law belongs to M_n only after stating that c_X<=1<=C_X and the Hölder radii contain its constant e=1/2 and m_0=2(1-t)d_n functions; ass:rare-event and ass:rate-compatibility alone do not imply those membership conditions.

soundness_flags.label: thm:diameter-upper
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed supremum has a right-hand side depending on the quantified P_n; state a pointwise bound for every P_n in M_n, or a normalized supremum such as sup_P E[diam(C)]/min{1,sqrt(kappa_n/(n d_n(P)))}<=C_alpha.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:diameter-lower
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The lower bound is obtained only on the covariate-homogeneous least-favorable submodel.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Conditional on the repaired membership lemma, it lower-bounds every procedure honest over any M_n containing that submodel; it is not yet a sharp converse over a broader covariate-rich model by itself.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair def:clipped-learners by fitting m_0 only in the control training sample, then restate and prove the weighted rate with the effective control sample size under overlap.
Make the model class an observed-law projection of an explicitly defined full-data extension class, and add the constant/radius conditions that make the least-favorable law a certified member.
Replace the McGrath--Burke failure attribution with its actual coverage/relative-margin comparison, and use Huwang1995 for the non-uniform normal-approximation claim.
Promote the score-cell likelihood-ratio OEQ into a concrete matched upper theorem by specifying its conditional experiment, intensities, and nuisance-stability argument against thm:diameter-lower.

recommended_next_step: Revise the learner definition, observed-law/full-data model class, least-favorable membership constants, and diameter-upper quantifier; then resubmit the repaired field-tier kernel.
